sentences.text: 2 . As per the complaint, the petitioner herein got acquaintance with the defacto complainant and borrowed money to the tune of Rs.42,00,000/- since 2016.
Further, the accused also subscribed one unauthorized chit run by the defacto complainant and drawn Rs.1,25,000/- and failed to repay it.

When the defacto complainant demanded back the money, the petitioner promised to repay it after disposing the property, but, breached the promise and later gave five cheques, promissory note and other documents.
3.
Later, when the defacto complainant demanded money the first and the second accused who were husband and wife threatened as if they got separated and not responsible for repayment.
At the same time, the first petitioner has transferred the house property in the name of the second petitioner in order to dispose it of to third parties and cheat the complainant.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that it is purely a https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis civil dispute in connection with money transaction which has been given a criminal colour and therefore, the same has to be quashed.
Further, referring the refusal of remand by the learned Judicial Magistrate, the learned counsel submits that it is purely a civil dispute which should not be proceeded as a criminal complaint.

5. This Court on perusing the F.I.R and the averment made in the petition finds that the complaint of breach of trust and cheating needs probe before arriving at any conclusive decision whether the ingredients to attract offences under Section 406 and 420 of IPC is made out.

Investigation is at nascent stage and the complaint discloses deception and entrustment whether that allegations are true and the deception was at inception of entrustment need probe and hence, the criminal original petition to quash the F.I.R stands dismissed as devoid of merits.
